title: Look as You Think: Unifying Reasoning and Visual Evidence Attribution for Verifiable Document RAG via Reinforcement Learning
research_question: Can a vision-language model be trained to produce accurate document-RAG answers while grounding intermediate reasoning steps and final answers to verifiable page-level visual regions with limited stepwise supervision?
methodology: The paper introduces Chain-of-Evidence, in which textual reasoning steps are paired with page indices and bounding boxes for their supporting evidence, followed by a final answer with its own supporting region. LAT uses two training stages: a cold-start stage creates CoE traces with Gemini 2.5 Pro from 1,000 sampled instances per training dataset, filters them for answer quality, manually corrects bounding-box drift, and performs LoRA supervised fine-tuning; a second stage applies GRPO reinforcement learning. The RL objective combines answer-accuracy, stepwise attribution, final grounding, and format rewards, including semantic comparison between reasoning steps and cropped evidence regions using ColQwen2. Experiments use Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct on Paper-VISA and Wiki-VISA under single-image, multi-image, in-domain, and cross-domain settings.

key_findings.finding: Across the reported single- and multi-image evaluations, LAT improves the vanilla model by an average of 8.23% in soft exact match and 47.0% in IoU@0.5.
In the in-domain comparison, LAT reports gains of 7.95% in answer exact match and 44.6% in IoU@0.5 over the vanilla model.
key_findings.section: 5.1 Attribution-aware performance under in-domain and cross-domain settings

key_findings.finding: LAT substantially improves stepwise Chain-of-Evidence attribution quality, with a reported 37.5% gain in stepwise attribution compared with only a 4.0% gain from adding an in-context CoE demonstration.
For unanswerable multi-image cases, LAT reports average precision of 65% when producing a no-answer response.
LAT outperforms the direct supervised answer-plus-attribution baseline and shows stronger cross-domain generalization in the reported experiments.
The Chain-of-Evidence representation records evidence at reasoning-step granularity as a page index plus a bounding box and separately grounds the final answer.

limitations: Thresholds used by the stepwise attribution rewards are manually selected from annotated examples rather than learned adaptively.
Training is currently limited to VISA data, whose evidence annotations are predominantly single-hop.
Generalization to multi-hop and cross-source evidence reasoning has not been fully evaluated or supervised.

The cold-start procedure depends on a proprietary Gemini 2.5 Pro model and subsequent manual bounding-box correction, which makes exact independent reproduction of the data-generation stage more involved.
raw_claims: Chain-of-Evidence associates reasoning steps with document page indices and visual bounding boxes.
The final answer is also paired with a page and supporting evidence box.
The cold-start stage samples 1,000 instances from each training dataset for CoE generation.
Gemini 2.5 Pro generates initial stepwise reasoning and evidence annotations.
The authors manually verify and correct bounding-box drift before cold-start supervised training.
LAT optimizes answer accuracy, stepwise evidence attribution, final grounding, and output-format objectives.
Stepwise evidence consistency is measured using representations of the reasoning text and the cropped document region.
Experiments cover both single-image and multi-image document inputs.
LAT reports average improvements of 8.23% in soft exact match and 47.0% in IoU@0.5 relative to the vanilla model.
The released implementation is linked to the PolarisLiu1/LAT GitHub repository.
The authors identify multi-hop and cross-source evidence reasoning as an unresolved direction.
